entries.note: No dashes, em dashes, or typical AI styling in any draft.
Don't open with 'been a minute' — use 'It's been a while since we last connected.'
CTA verb: 'surf' beats 'ride' — 'get you out for a surf'.
Forward-looking only — don't reference old activities or past interactions (e.g. 'we talked about a factory tour a while back' is banned).
Avoid phrasing that makes the customer sound like a member of a group ('Arizona folks') — say what the business is doing instead ('we're kicking up demos in AZ soon').
Region personalization is welcome but must be grounded in real, confirmed activity — never invent a location or date.
Drop 'Want me to pencil you in?' as the closing CTA — reads as an immediate scheduling ask. Use a lighter 'You interested?' instead.

Approved sample style for a location-announcement campaign: 'Hey {First}, it's Nick with Arc. We've got demos coming up at [locations]. Would love to get you out for a surf. You interested?' — short, 1-2 sentences, no dashes.

Supplied exact copy for the Sausalito September campaign and chose to KEEP the hyphen in 'Booking Link - https://...' verbatim, overriding the standing no-dashes rule. A user-supplied template wins over the style rule when he says keep it verbatim.

Tahoe exclusion: exclude leads who themselves mention Tahoe, have Tahoe notes, or demoed there. Do NOT exclude on our own outbound boilerplate that pitched 'Tahoe and Sausalito' as a pair, that is us talking not them. For prospecting_tahoe Meta-ad-sourced leads, exclude only the ones outside the Bay Area.
